---
title: "Recipes"
---

Five complete, copyable setups: a personal blog, a project portfolio, a
documentation book, a standalone talk, and a single long-form post. Each one shows
the directory layout, the config, and the key front matter, with notes on the parts
that bite. Copy the closest one and edit it down.

Every key used below is real. If you want the full list of what each one does, the
[front matter](../reference/frontmatter.qmd), [cell options](../reference/cell-options.qmd),
and [configuration](../reference/configuration.qmd) references are the source of truth;
this page is the "here is a working whole" companion to them.

## 1. A personal blog

> A home page that lists recent posts, a `blog.qmd` index over a `posts/` folder,
> and an `about.qmd` profile, all generated from front matter.

```text
blog/
├── _site.yml
├── index.qmd            # home: about header + "recent posts" listing
├── blog.qmd             # the full post index (a grid)
├── about.qmd            # a profile page
├── profile.webp
├── favicon.svg
└── posts/
    ├── first-post/
    │   ├── index.qmd
    │   └── thumbnail.webp
    └── second-post/
        └── index.qmd
```

A post is its own folder so its images and any `.bib` live next to it. Page
discovery walks the whole tree, so `posts/first-post/index.qmd` is a real page; the
listing crawls the same folder to build the cards.

The project config, `_site.yml`:

```yaml
title: "Jane Doe"
description: "Notes on things I'm learning"
url: "https://example.com"
favicon: favicon.svg
toc: true
nav:
  - { text: Blog, href: blog.qmd }
  - { text: About, href: about.qmd }
footer:
  left: "© 2026 Jane Doe"
  right:
    - { icon: github, href: "https://github.com/jane" }
```

The home page leads with an `about:` header and fills a `listing:` with the two most
recent posts. The `id:` makes the listing fill a `::: {#recent}` block where you put
it, instead of appending to the end of the page:

```yaml
---
title: "Jane Doe"
about:
  template: jolla
  image: profile.webp
  image-alt: "Jane Doe"
toc: false
listing:
  id: recent
  contents: posts
  sort: "date desc"
  max-items: 3
  type: grid
---

I write about things I am working to understand.

## Recent posts

::: {#recent}
:::

[View all posts →](blog.qmd)
```

The full index, `blog.qmd`, is a listing with nothing else on the page. `page-layout:
full` widens the column so the card grid breathes, and `title-block-style: none`
keeps the title metadata (for the tab and social card) while hiding the big visible
`<h1>`:

```yaml
---
title: "Blog"
title-block-style: none
page-layout: full
listing:
  contents: posts
  sort: "date desc"
  type: grid
  categories: true
---
```

`categories: true` adds a clickable filter row built from the `categories:` on each
post. Each post supplies what the card shows through its own front matter:

```yaml
---
title: "My first post"
description: "What it's about, in one sentence."
date: 2026-05-08
image: "thumbnail.webp"
categories: [machine learning, statistics]
---
```

::: {.callout-note}
`sort: "date desc"` is the default; write `"date asc"` for oldest-first. A post with
no `date:` still appears, but undated posts cluster deterministically at one end (last
under `date desc`, first under `date asc`) and ties break on file path, so give every
post a date if order matters.
:::

## 2. A project / portfolio site

> A `hero:` landing page, a nav bar, and a `projects.qmd` index that lists each
> project.

```text
portfolio/
├── _site.yml
├── index.qmd            # hero landing
├── projects.qmd         # a listing over projects/
├── favicon.svg
└── projects/
    ├── thing-one/
    │   ├── index.qmd
    │   └── shot.webp
    └── thing-two/
        └── index.qmd
```

`_site.yml`:

```yaml
title: "Jane Doe"
description: "Things I build"
favicon: favicon.svg
nav:
  left:
    - { text: Projects, href: projects.qmd }
  right:
    - { icon: github, href: "https://github.com/jane" }
    - { icon: linkedin, href: "https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane" }
footer:
  left: "© 2026 Jane Doe"
```

The landing page uses a `hero:` block: a big headline, a lead sentence, and a row of
call-to-action buttons. `headline:` falls back to `title:` if you omit it, and each
action is `{ text, href, primary }` (mark one `primary: true` to make it the filled
button):

```yaml
---
title: "Jane Doe"
hero:
  eyebrow: "Software & research"
  headline: "I build tools for thinking."
  lead: "Interactive explainers, dev tooling, and the occasional paper."
  actions:
    - { text: "See my work", href: "projects.qmd", primary: true }
    - { text: "GitHub", href: "https://github.com/jane" }
---

A paragraph or two below the hero, if you like. Everything after the front matter
renders as normal page content.
```

`projects.qmd` is the same listing pattern as the blog index, pointed at `projects/`:

```yaml
---
title: "Projects"
title-block-style: none
page-layout: full
listing:
  contents: projects
  sort: "date desc"
  type: grid
  categories: true
---

Things I built to learn something.
```

::: {.callout-tip}
The nav and footer accept a bundled icon glyph (`{ icon: github, href: … }`) instead
of raw HTML. Available glyphs: `github`, `linkedin`, `rss`, `x`, `mastodon`,
`bluesky`, `email`. For anything else, pass an inline `<svg>` as the item `text:`.
:::

## 3. A documentation book

> Numbered chapters grouped into a part, a sidebar table of contents, and Cmd-K
> search, all from one `chapters:` list.

```text
handbook/
├── _site.yml
├── index.qmd            # the cover / preface
├── intro.qmd
├── setup.qmd
├── usage.qmd
└── reference.qmd
```

The presence of `chapters:` in `_site.yml` is what makes the project a book: no
`type:` key needed. qmd-fast numbers the chapters, builds the left sidebar, wires
prev/next navigation, and resolves cross-references across chapters. A chapter entry
is a bare filename, a `{ part:, chapters: }` group header, or a `{ file:, text: }`
mapping whose `text:` overrides the sidebar label:

```yaml
title: "The Handbook"
author: "Jane Doe"
toc: true
chapters:
  - index.qmd
  - intro.qmd
  - part: "Using it"
    chapters:
      - setup.qmd
      - file: usage.qmd       # { file:, text: } overrides the sidebar label
        text: "Everyday use"
  - reference.qmd
```

`toc: true` gives each chapter a live, scrollspy table of contents, and the Cmd-K
(Ctrl-K) search palette indexes every chapter. The book output directory defaults to
`_book/` instead of `_site/`. The chapter pages themselves need no special front
matter; a plain `title:` is enough:

```yaml
---
title: "Introduction"
---
```

Without an explicit `text:` override, the sidebar label is the chapter's first `#`
heading, then its front-matter `title:`, then the file name. These very docs are a
book built this way: look at the sidebar and press Cmd-K to try the search.

::: {.callout-note}
There is no `_metadata.yml` cascade. The root `_site.yml` sets defaults (like
`toc:`) and a chapter's own front matter overrides them, two levels, no directory
merge. See [Slides, books & sites](formats.qmd) for the difference between a book and
a plain multi-page site.
:::

## 4. A talk (a standalone deck, embedded in notes)

> A self-contained slide deck (`format: revealjs`), plus a notes page that embeds it
> with `{{< embed >}}`.

```text
talk/
├── _site.yml
├── index.qmd            # the talk's companion notes page
└── slides.qmd           # the deck itself (format: revealjs)
```

The deck is a normal document with `format: revealjs`. `##` starts a slide, `#`
starts a section that nests the following slides as a vertical stack, and a title
slide is generated from the metadata:

```markdown
---
title: "My talk"
subtitle: "A live demo"
format: revealjs
---

## First slide

- a point
- another point

## A diagram slide

Some prose, then a chart or image.
```

The notes page embeds the deck inline as an isolating, interactive iframe with a
fullscreen button. The deck is built and served automatically as a dependency of the
page; it does not show up in the nav or search (it is an inclusion, not a page):

```markdown
---
title: "Talk notes"
---

Here are the slides, then the long-form notes.

{{< embed slides.qmd title="My talk" >}}

## Notes

The points I didn't have room for on the slides go here.
```

`_site.yml` lists only the notes page; the deck is reached through the embed:

```yaml
title: "My talk"
nav:
  - { text: Notes, href: index.qmd }
```

::: {.callout-important}
`{{< embed >}}` only builds its target during a **site** build (`qmd-fast build
<dir>`). A single-doc build (`qmd-fast build index.qmd`) does *not* build the embedded
deck and will warn. To present the deck on its own instead, point the command
straight at it: `qmd-fast preview slides.qmd` or `qmd-fast build slides.qmd`. See
[Slides, books & sites](formats.qmd) for the deck engine's features (speaker view,
fragments, PDF export).
:::

## 5. A single long-form technical post

> One `.qmd` file with math, citations from a `.bib`, and numbered, cross-referenced
> figures. No `_site.yml`, no directory: just a file you preview and build directly.

```text
post/
├── article.qmd
├── references.bib
└── diagram.svg
```

This is the simplest project of all: a lone document. Preview it with
`qmd-fast preview article.qmd` and build it with `qmd-fast build article.qmd` (which
produces one self-contained `.html`). The front matter pulls in the bibliography and
sets the metadata:

```yaml
---
title: "A geometric view of the thing"
subtitle: "Why the obvious approach is wrong"
author: "Jane Doe"
date: 2026-06-01
description: "One sentence for the social card."
toc: true
bibliography: references.bib
---
```

`bibliography:` enables `[@key]` citations and appends an auto-generated References
section. (References always render in a single built-in IEEE style; a `csl:` key is
accepted but not currently honored.) Inline and display math use `$…$` and `$$…$$`,
rendered server-side, so the HTML carries the math with no client-side library:

```markdown
The estimator minimizes the squared error $\lVert y - X\beta \rVert^2$. Its closed
form follows from setting the gradient to zero [@hastie2009]:

$$ \hat{\beta} = (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top y. $$ {#eq-ols}

As @eq-ols shows, the fit is linear in $y$.
```

Give a display equation `{#eq-name}` and reference it as `@eq-ols`. The same numbered
cross-reference scheme covers figures (`@fig-`) and sections (`@sec-`); a reference
to a label that does not exist is reported by `check`. A static image becomes a
numbered figure with a Markdown caption and an `{#fig-shape}` id:

```markdown
![A standardized data cloud with its principal axes.](diagram.svg){#fig-shape}

@fig-shape shows the axes lining up with the directions of greatest variance.
```

::: {.callout-note}
The cross-reference label and its target must live in the **same document**. For a
figure produced by a code cell instead of a static image, set the cell's `#| label:
fig-…` and `#| fig-cap: "…"` options; see [Running code](code.qmd) and
[Writing](writing.qmd) for the figure and citation details.
:::
